source: CFBD /conferences: 201 Western Conference (1896-1952) and 5 Big Ten (1953-)
notes: The Western Conference is the Big Ten under its pre-1953 CFBD label: one body.

The AAWU (1959) was renamed Pacific-8 (1968), Pacific-10 (1978) and Pac-12 (2011): one lineage. The two-member Pac-12 of 2024-25 (Oregon State, Washington State) and the rebuilt eight-member Pac-12 of 2026 keep CFBD and ESPN id 9, so they stay in it.
The PCC dissolved in 1959, and the AAWU that followed is a new body (cfb:pac-12), so the PCC keeps its own lineage.
The Big Six grew into the Big Seven (1948) and the Big Eight (1958): one body. The 1996 Big 12 is a new body (cfb:big-12).
A new body in 1996 (the Big Eight plus four Southwest Conference schools), not a continuation of cfb:big-eight.

source: CFBD /conferences: 202 Missouri Valley Intercollegiate Athletic Association (1907-1927)
notes: Kept apart from the Missouri Valley Conference (cfb:missouri-valley) and the Big Six (cfb:big-eight). Both later bodies claim it, and CFBD names it separately.

American Athletic Conference (2013), renamed American Conference (2025): one lineage. It is legally the successor of the original Big East, but CFBD and ESPN both mint new ids, so football's Big East is its own lineage (cfb:big-east, 1991-2012).
The football Big East (1991-2012).

One body. WAC football was FBS through 2012, then dropped football, then returned as FCS in 2021-22 before merging into the UAC. ESPN files group 16 under FCS (81) in every season; the parent here comes from CFBD's classification instead: FBS through 2012, FCS in 2021-22.
The 2021 ASUN-WAC Challenge scheduling alliance. CFBD and ESPN both carry it as a conference.
The United Athletic Conference: the ASUN-WAC football merger. A new body (both sources mint new ids).
The Pacific Coast Athletic Association was renamed the Big West Conference in 1988.

source: CFBD /conferences: 298 Gateway Collegiate (1985-91); 299 Gateway Football (1992-2007); 21 MVFC; ESPN group 21
notes: The Gateway was renamed the Missouri Valley Football Conference in 2008. CFBD already files some Gateway-era spells under 21.

The Colonial League was renamed the Patriot League in 1990.
The Mid-American Conference. CFBD's 1948-49 tier split (342) folds in.

The A-10 took over Yankee Conference football in 1997 and handed it to the CAA in 2007. The sponsoring conference changed each time and both sources mint new ids, so cfb:yankee, cfb:atlantic-10 and cfb:caa are separate lineages.
A different body from the D-III Heartland Collegiate Athletic Conference (111, cfb:heartland), which CFBD gives the same short name.
The Southern California Intercollegiate Athletic Conference under two CFBD labels.
